subject: TNF inhibitors: tuberculosis reporting is 7.5× the rest of FAERS
headline: TNF inhibitors: tuberculosis reporting is 7.5× the rest of FAERS
intro: This is the first briefing, from the snapshot of 15 October 2026. There is no earlier snapshot to compare, so the lists below are the latest notices and the strongest prespecified signals in the current extract, not week-over-week changes. openFDA extract dated 2026-07-30. Myocardial Infarction and Cerebrovascular Accident cleared a reporting-odds bound only. The PRR is below 2, so those comparisons are not Evans signals and they are not the headline. PRR and ROR describe how often a reaction is reported. They are not incidence and they are not proof a drug caused an event.

disclaimer: Inflammation Signal Monitor is for research and public-health surveillance. It is not medical advice, and it does not estimate how often an adverse reaction occurs or prove that a drug caused it. FAERS is a spontaneous-report system with under-reporting, duplicate reports, and no exposure denominator. Do not start or stop a medicine based on this site. Talk with a clinician. Report adverse events to FDA MedWatch.

items.title: TNF inhibitors · Tuberculosis
items.body: In this extract, tuberculosis is reported with TNF inhibitors 7.54 times as often as with all other FAERS reports (PRR 7.54, 95% CI 7.28–7.82). The reporting odds ratio is 7.56 (95% CI 7.29–7.84). This meets the Evans screen: at least 3 reports, a PRR of at least 2, and a chi-square of at least 4. A ratio like this is not proof the drug caused the event, and it is not an incidence rate.
